The 5,593 teu HMM Platinum suffered a fire while sailing from Kattupalli, India, towards Santos, Brazil. The blaze reportedly originated in a container off southern Madagascar. Claims specialist W.E. Cox said the Liberian-flagged ship, built in 2013, was carrying around 2,300 containers and warned that damage could be substantial. Salvage specialist SMIT has been engaged under LOF terms, while a declaration of general average is considered likely. The vessel was initially expected to divert to Durban, with an anticipated arrival on October 8. candidates.excerpt: Singapore-listed First Ship Lease Trust (FSL) has agreed to sell another ageing product tanker, continuing a series of disposals that has reduced its fleet over recent years. The trust said in a filing that subsidiary FSL-14 had struck a deal to sell the 2006-built Speciality to an unrelated buyer. The 4,426 dwt tanker was built at Qingshan Shipyard in China. The purchaser has lodged a 10% deposit in escrow, although FSL has not disclosed the agreed price or the buyer’s identity. Further transaction details will be released when the sale is completed. The vessel had been employed under a bareboat charter with UK shipping group James Fisher, a longstanding FSL customer. FSL’s latest fleet information shows that Speciality was returned to the trust in May 2026 and subsequently entered drydock. candidates.excerpt: AI fears, not fundamentals, behind software markdowns Unrealised losses in private credit have been a headwind to total returns, with recent markdowns concentrated in software, but these reflect uncertainty over AI rather than weakening fundamentals, according to BlackRock. Markdowns on software loans have accounted for roughly two-thirds of total unrealised losses in the asset class since the fourth quarter of 2025, BlackRock’s latest quarterly private credit outlook found. The weighted average valuation of first-lien software loans fell from near par at the end of 2025 to around 97 per cent of cost in the second quarter of 2026, while moves in other sectors were far more modest. Media and entertainment loans saw the next-largest markdowns, followed by consumer services, according to Cliffwater Direct Lending Index data cited by the asset manager. candidates.title: Private credit growth piles pressure on valuations
candidates.excerpt: Private credit growth piles pressure on valuations Private credit is being priced more often as it expands into funds sold to retail investors, but only a handful of fund groups fully revalue the loans each day, according to Deloitte. Deloitte’s 24th Fair Valuation Pricing Survey, which polled more than 100 fund groups, found that 48 per cent now refresh private credit valuations daily using observable market inputs. However, just 4 per cent carry out a full daily update that revisits unobservable inputs, cash flow assumptions and methodology. The largest share, 39 per cent, do so quarterly. A third of fund groups surveyed now hold private credit, and 66 per cent of those increased their positions over the past year. The shift reflects the asset class moving beyond closed-ended institutional funds and into products that must publish a price every day. candidates.excerpt: ASIC halts offers in three more private credit funds Australia’s corporate regulator has halted offers in three more private credit funds managed by Australian Secure Capital Fund (ASCF), as troubles mount in the sector. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) said in a statement that it had made an interim stop order on the product disclosure statement (PDS) for the ASCF Premium Capital Fund, ASCF Select Income Fund and ASCF High Yield Fund.
